id.description: Citation marker as it appears in the paper (e.g. '1', '12', 'Smith2020')

relation.description: How this reference relates to the citing paper, judged from in-text citation context.

roles.description: Functional role(s) this reference plays for the citing paper; one or more. extends=a direct predecessor THIS paper's contribution builds on, improves, or extends (the cited method your work descends from); uses_component=a method/architecture/algorithm/technique/tool/optimizer/library/dataset/benchmark reused as a building block, not the contribution's lineage; compares=compared against experimentally (a baseline) or critiqued/disagreed with (the `stance` field carries supportive/neutral/critical); background=field/concept context, motivation, future-work mention, or passing related mention. When ambiguous between extends and background, prefer extends if the cited work is plausibly a direct predecessor (high recall); use background only when no stronger role fits.

stance.description: How the citing paper positions itself: builds on it (supportive), neutral mention, or critiques/contrasts it (critical). Default neutral when unclear.

salience.description: central = load-bearing for this paper's argument or experiments (a main baseline, a core building block, or relied on repeatedly); peripheral = passing mention.

provides_name.description: For extends, uses_component, and compares, the single most specific named artifact the citing paper takes from or compares against this work (e.g. 'Transformer', 'ImageNet', 'Adam', 'BERT'). Empty string for background or when no concrete artifact is named.

provides_unit_ids.description: Always output an empty array []. Links to spine unit IDs are filled deterministically by the pipeline after section extraction; never populate this yourself.
